Upstream imports this inner SDK package only for five OAuth validation schemas used on stored grant and client records; in Go those records are validated by harness-owned types and the protocol types come from the single Go SDK module.

Test-only glue that adapts the TypeScript SDK's web-standard HTTP handler to Node's http module for fixtures; it exists only because of Node. The Go SDK's HTTP server is already a net/http handler, so no adapter has a counterpart.

Version 1 of the TypeScript SDK is declared by subagent-claude-code only to satisfy the npm peer dependency of the Claude Agent SDK (pnpm-lock.yaml:20917) and is never imported by upstream source; it exists only because of npm peer-dependency resolution, which Go modules do not have.

title: Two generations of the MCP TypeScript SDK are installed side by side: 2.x split packages for harness code and 1.31.0 only as a peer of the Claude Agent SDK and the reference servers
The MCP bridge imports the SDK's inner core package and depends on exact pins of an SDK its README calls still evolving
The SDK, not the host, spawns the stdio MCP child, and negotiation may start a temporary probe process before the serving process
Bridge workarounds for SDK behaviour: a stdout-writing fallback, a repeated output-schema check, aborts reported as timeouts, and replaced transport methods to observe closure
The Computer Use MCP server is built on a deprecated low-level SDK class and deprecated elicitation accessors behind lint suppressions
@playwright/mcp is an exactly pinned 0.0.x package that installs a second, alpha build of Playwright beside the workspace's own
The inspector maintains its own build of a pinned Chrome DevTools source snapshot with hand-written substitutes for generated inputs

reason: One Go module in one version serves the client role, the server role and the fixtures, and Go has no peer-dependency mechanism that could force a second generation into the build.
Exactly one harness package imports the SDK and exposes harness types; stored OAuth records are validated by harness types, so an SDK upgrade is neither a data migration nor a change to callers.
The harness process service starts the one child and passes only its pipes to the SDK; the Go SDK negotiates the revision on that same connection, so no probe process is started.

The harness interface returns a closed set of error kinds and an explicit close result, every request carries a harness deadline so deadline and cancellation are told apart locally, and stdout cleanliness is a test instead of a workaround.

The Go SDK's ordinary server supports adding and removing tools at run time, and a consent question returned as an input request is served to clients on revision 2026-07-28 and on older revisions, so no deprecated API is needed.
The browser MCP server leaves the harness's dependency graph: it is an external program with its own dependencies, found on the operator's machine and version-checked when it connects.
The Go harness does not build or ship the Chrome DevTools interface, so there is no source snapshot to track and no substitute build inputs to maintain.
